name: Ares
description: Dreadnode's Rust multi-agent platform that chains impacket, NetExec and certipy against Active Directory; it ships its own detections
seenIn: No public report of use in an attack. Covered from its source code

indicators.context: Fixed PFX passphrase Ares' pywhisker wrapper sets with --pfx-password on every Shadow Credentials export, and passes again as certipy auth -password ares-shadow-cred (ares-tools/src/acl.rs:262,479; privesc/adcs.rs:297)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Ares source code

indicators.context: Prefix of every Shadow Credentials export Ares asks pywhisker to write: <temp>/ares_shadowcred_<epoch ms>-<pid>-<seq>_<account> (.pfx, _cert.pem, _priv.pem), then read by certipy auth -pfx (ares-tools/src/acl.rs:270,409-418)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Ares source code

indicators.context: Prefix of every machine account Ares adds with impacket-addcomputer: ARES- plus 8 uppercase hex digits and a trailing $, password Ar<16 hex>!7z; the name is minted in code whatever the model asks for (privesc/delegation.rs:362-378). Match the full pattern ^ARES-[0-9A-F]{8}\$$, not the prefix alone
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Ares source code

indicators.context: Name prefix of the immediate scheduled task Ares pushes through a writable GPO with pygpoabuse: ARES_GPO_Probe_<8 hex>, command cmd /c whoami, -f (orchestrator/automation/gpo.rs:143-160,366-377)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Ares source code

indicators.context: Delimiter rows (___ARES_HIVE_SAM_B64___, ___ARES_HIVE_SYSTEM_B64___, ___ARES_HIVE_SECURITY_B64___ and the _END___ forms) around the base64 SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives in Ares' xp_cmdshell hive dump; seen in PowerShell script block logs and SQL result sets (lateral/mssql.rs:345-385)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Ares source code

indicators.context: Start of the -EncodedCommand of Ares' far-host hive dump (powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand ...), run by xp_cmdshell on a linked SQL Server. The script has no variables, so the whole base64 is the same on every run (lateral/mssql.rs:368-385,494-496)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Ares source code
